findings.claim: The user_location cleanup in deleteLocation only covers the location passed in, so purging a parent location whose descendant is assigned to a user still dies on the same user_location FK the hunk exists to work around.
findings.failure_mode: If merged as-is, LocationService.purgeLocation(parent) throws org.hibernate.exception.ConstraintViolationException ("USER_LOCATION FOREIGN KEY(LOCATION_ID) REFERENCES LOCATION(LOCATION_ID)") whenever any descendant of that location is in user_location, because Location.childLocations is mapped @OneToMany(cascade = CascadeType.ALL, orphanRemoval = true) (api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/Location.java:140) so session.remove(parent) issues a delete for every child row, while the native delete above it only removes user_location rows for location.getLocationId(). This is the ticket's own usage model: TRUNK-6669 says "admin UI expands a parent department to its children on assignment; user_location stores the resolved leaf rows", so the assigned rows are always leaves and the purgeable object is the parent department. Recommended fix: put onDelete="CASCADE" on the user_location_to_location FK in this PR's own (not yet shipped) changeset -- core already uses onDelete="CASCADE" in liquibase-update-to-latest-2.4.x.xml (concept_complex, concept_numeric, patient, test_order) and 2.5.x, it drops the native delete and its session-cache caveat comment entirely, and it covers every path that deletes a location row rather than just LocationDAO.deleteLocation. If the project prefers to keep RESTRICT, the delete has to span the descendant subtree, and this same class already has the recursive-CTE descendant query to reuse (HibernateLocationDAO.getDescendantIds, line ~470).
findings.evidence: Reproduced in the worktree at b7cd909d245086fa10691496f88e5ec6971b77c2 with a positive control, then reverted (git status --porcelain clean). Added two temporary tests to api/src/test/java/org/openmrs/api/LocationServiceTest.java, each creating a fresh parent+child location (so no unrelated FK interferes) and flushing/clearing the session between steps. Ran: JAVA_HOME=/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/jdk-21.jdk/Contents/Home mvn -o -pl api test -Dtest='LocationServiceTest#zzControl_purgeFreshParentNoUserAssignment+zzGap_purgeFreshParentWhoseChildIsAssignedToUser'. Control (no user assignment) PASSED -- purging the parent cascade-deletes the child cleanly. Gap test (child assigned to user 1, then purge the parent) FAILED: 'org.hibernate.exception.ConstraintViolationException: could not execute batch [Referential integrity constraint violation: "FKC0WEUGWTYIDBYTMDYE09CP0GL: PUBLIC.USER_LOCATION FOREIGN KEY(LOCATION_ID) REFERENCES PUBLIC.LOCATION(LOCATION_ID) (11)"]' -- id 11 is the child, not the purged parent. An earlier variant that kept the User loaded in the session instead produced 'TransientPropertyValueException: Persistent instance of org.openmrs.User references an unsaved transient instance of org.openmrs.Location [org.openmrs.User.locations -> org.openmrs.Location]', i.e. the session-cache caveat the comment at line 129-132 calls "safe today since no caller holds a loaded User across this call" is reachable from the same call. Cascade mechanism read at api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/Location.java:140 (jakarta.persistence.CascadeType imported at line 18). CASCADE precedent verified by git grep 'onDelete="CASCADE"' over api/src/main/resources/org/openmrs/liquibase/updates. Mirror case checked and clean: a temporary UserServiceTest probe purging a user who has assigned locations passes (Hibernate deletes the owned collection rows first), so only the location side needs work.

findings.claim: getAllowedLocations resolves the tag through LocationService.getLocationsByTag, the one tag query in this codebase that loads every unretired location and filters in Java, rather than either of the two single-query paths the tree already maintains -- including the exact method the endpoint this feature replaces calls.
findings.evidence: Measured, not inferred. Temporary probe in LocationServiceTest (since reverted; git status --porcelain clean) enabled Hibernate statistics and ran all three paths for the same one-tag query on the LocationServiceTest dataset (6 unretired locations, 1 tagged). Output: getLocationsByTag results=1 stmts=2 entities=11 collFetches=1; getLocationsHavingAllTags results=1 stmts=1 entities=1 collFetches=0; getLocations(LocationSearchCriteria) results=1 stmts=1 entities=1 collFetches=0. The 11 entities are all 6 Locations plus their LocationTags -- the cost scales with the total location count, not the tagged count, because LocationServiceImpl.getLocationsByTag (api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/impl/LocationServiceImpl.java:213-221) is 'for (Location l : dao.getAllLocations(false)) if (l.getTags().contains(tag))'. Sibling check: the endpoint TRUNK-6669 says the frontend will replace, GET /ws/rest/v1/location?tag=Login+Location, calls getLocationsHavingAllTags -- read at omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs1_8/LocationResource1_8.java:311 on openmrs-module-webservices.rest master. Direction check: LocationSearchCriteria is the newest location-query API (@since 2.8.7, LocationService.java:407), does the tag filter in SQL with join+groupBy+having and name ordering and paging (HibernateLocationDAO.addTagPredicates / applyPagination, lines 511-536), and the two commits immediately preceding this PR on HibernateLocationDAO are the ones that built it and then tuned it for performance (11607283d6 TRUNK-6635, 9e011e2c09 TRUNK-6681 'Improve LocationSearchCriteria query performance with pagination'). Criteria objects are the established shape for a new filtered query here: org/openmrs/parameter holds Concept/Encounter/Location/MedicationDispense/Obs/Order/Visit search criteria. Dormancy check with positive control: git grep getLocationsByTag at merge base 28e3bab9e206170df7fd43cf709495b6d45fe16a over api/src returns only its own declaration, its impl and two tests -- zero production callers before this PR -- while the same grep for getLocationsHavingAllTags returns a DAO layer, a service layer and DAO+service tests. Recommended default: build a LocationSearchCriteria with setLocationTags(Collections.singleton(tag)) and call LocationService.getLocations(criteria) -- one statement, name-ordered like the current path, and composable with the nameFragment/includeRetired/descendantOf/paging filters the companion 'forCurrentUser' location search will otherwise have to re-filter in Java. Secondary cost of the service-layer-composition shape: because the intersection is done on hydrated entities rather than in SQL, the impl has to defensively re-read the user (dao.getUser(user.getUserId()) at line 860) with a comment explaining why; a userId-keyed DAO query would need neither.

findings.claim: Is enforcement meant to be out of scope? getAllowedLocations is a read filter with nothing in core stopping a restricted user from using a location outside their assignment, which the PR title ("restricting users to assigned locations") and the "locations the given user is allowed to use" javadoc both read as stronger than.
findings.evidence: UserContext.setLocation(Location) and UserContext.setLocationId(Integer) are public and unguarded (api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/context/UserContext.java:578 and :597), and nothing consults User.locations on that path -- git grep getAllowedLocations over api/src/main finds only the declaration and its impl, so there is no in-core enforcement caller. TRUNK-6669's acceptance criteria are all about what the GET returns, so the PR matches the ticket and I am not asking for enforcement here; the ask is one javadoc sentence saying this resolves a picker list and is not an access check, so module authors do not build authorization on it. Asking rather than asserting because the follow-up-ticket question is the author's and the community thread's to answer.

what_i_swept: Verified the stat first: git diff 28e3bab9e206170df7fd43cf709495b6d45fe16a b7cd909d245086fa10691496f88e5ec6971b77c2 is 8 files, +216/-6, matching. Read TRUNK-6669 with its two comments via the unauthenticated JIRA REST endpoint and the PR title/body/metadata (no review conversation read, per the constraint), then ran Step 2 in full against them. Problem: every Login Location is shown to every user at /login/location, and there is no standard way to associate a user with a subset of locations; the ticket's core-side asks are a user_location join table modelled on user_role, a service method returning the tag-intersection with an unrestricted fallback, and no behavioural change where user_location is empty. Does it resolve that: yes for the core half -- ran the author's five new getAllowedLocations tests on JDK 21 (the task's JDK 8 hint is wrong for this repo, pom sets maven.compiler.release=21) and all five pass, covering the unrestricted fallback, the intersection, the empty intersection, a transient user and a null tag. Does it do only that: accounted for all 8 hunks. User.locations + accessors, UserService/UserServiceImpl.getAllowedLocations, the liquibase changeset, the two test classes and the DatabaseUpdaterDatabaseIT 916->917 bump are all required; the HibernateLocationDAO.deleteLocation hunk is required because the new FK otherwise breaks the existing purgeLocation API (my own repro produced that exact violation); the LOCATION_ID constant extraction touches 3 pre-existing lines but the merge-base file already had exactly 3 "locationId" literals, so the new :locationId parameter is what tripped the duplicate-literal gate -- there is no better alternative than extracting it, so no finding. Nothing extra to take out: the liquibase file is appended to only, and the changeset id follows the TRUNK-nnnn-YYYY-MM-DD convention of its 12 siblings in that file. Is it the best fix available: compared against the nearest siblings rather than general practice -- user_role for the mapping (matched, including the composite PK and no audit columns, and preferred over the ticket's own surrogate-id SQL), @Independent on Location.tags and OrderType for the RequiredDataAdvice opt-out (matched; it is also what stops RequiredDataAdvice retiring a user's locations when the user is retired, so it is load-bearing beyond the LazyInitializationException the PR body cites), Context.getXService() from inside UserServiceImpl (established, 12 existing uses), and getLocationsHavingAllTags / LocationSearchCriteria for the tag query (diverged -- finding 2). Also positively verified that core has no pre-existing mechanism this re-implements: no location column on the users table in the 2.9 schema snapshot, no Set<Location> on any core entity before this PR, and USER_PROPERTY_DEFAULT_LOCATION is a single default location consumed by UserContext.getDefaultLocationId, not a permitted set. Outward traces: (1) the delete path one level out from deleteLocation, through LocationServiceImpl.purgeLocation into Hibernate's cascade on Location.childLocations -- this is where finding 1 came from; (2) the mirror path, purging a User who has assigned locations, probed empirically and clean; (3) the consumer, the companion webservices.rest PR -- read LocationResource1_8.doSearch on that repo's master to establish what the endpoint being replaced actually calls, which is what prices finding 2; (4) the criteria-object neighbours in org/openmrs/parameter and the two commits that immediately precede this PR on HibernateLocationDAO, to establish the tree's current direction; (5) Envers -- User is @Audited and the new collection is not @NotAudited, but hibernate.integration.envers.enabled=false by default and no *_audit tables exist in liquibase for user_role either, so locations matches its sibling and there is no finding; (6) the session-location lifecycle in UserContext, which is where finding 3 came from. Three passes: pass 1 surfaced finding 2, pass 2 surfaced finding 1 (so pass 2 could not be last), pass 3 turned up only supporting evidence (criteria-object breadth, the zero-production-callers result, the Envers dead end) and no new substantive finding.
out_of_scope: Correctness: User.setLocations(null) is still permitted, so getLocations() can return null despite the field's empty-set initialisation and the javadoc contract; getAllowedLocations defends with an 'assigned == null' check but external callers of getLocations() do not.

Correctness: the native delete in deleteLocation runs before session.remove(location), and its own comment concedes a loaded User.locations collection in the same session will not reflect the removal -- my probe hit exactly that as a TransientPropertyValueException when a User was held across the call.

Correctness/serialization: User is Serializable and held in UserContext (and hence the HTTP session), and locations is the first LAZY collection on it (roles is EAGER) -- worth checking what an uninitialized PersistentSet does under servlet session serialization.

Performance: User is @Cacheable with @Cache(READ_WRITE) and roles carries its own @Cache, but locations carries none, so every getAllowedLocations call loads the collection from the DB even on a second-level-cache hit.
Performance: user_location has no standalone index on location_id (the composite PK is user_id first), which the PR's own 'delete from user_location where location_id = ?' scans on.

Security/authorization: getAllowedLocations is guarded by GET_LOCATIONS only, yet it discloses which locations a named user is assigned to; whether GET_USERS should also be required is an authorization call.
Conventions: @Authorized is duplicated on both the interface declaration and the impl method; only one other UserServiceImpl method (line 648) does that, the rest rely on the interface.

Conventions: the new changeset is the only one in liquibase-update-to-latest-3.0.x.xml with a preConditions block; MARK_RAN on tableExists means a distro that already has a user_location table silently skips the changeset and may end up with a schema that does not match the mapping.
could_not_verify: The companion openmrs-module-webservices.rest PR #762 -- I read LocationResource1_8.doSearch on that repo's master to establish what today's tag endpoint calls, but did not review the PR itself, so I cannot say whether it resolves the tag by name, adds proxy privileges, or combines the restriction with other location filters.

Whether the REST session endpoint lets a restricted user set an arbitrary sessionLocation -- I could not locate SessionResource in that repo's tree listing, so finding 3 is grounded only on UserContext.setLocation/setLocationId being public and unguarded in core, and ships as a question rather than an assertion.

Real-world location counts. The entity-load measurement in finding 2 is exact for the 6-location test dataset and the mechanism makes it scale with total locations, but I have no figure for how many locations a real multi-department deployment carries, so the size of the effect on a production login is unquantified.

The unsaved-LocationTag edge on the recommended criteria path: I verified getLocations(LocationSearchCriteria) is equivalent for a persisted tag, and read addTagPredicates to see that a one-element list containing a null id is not empty and so still yields an in(null) predicate, but I did not run that case.
